questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating a Logarithmic Function With a General Base
questions.worked_solution:
To differentiate a logarithm with base $a,$ we use the formula

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{a}⁡x)=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡a}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({2}^{x}+\operatorname{log}⁡x) \\  & ={2}^{x}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡2+\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡10} \\  & ={2}^{x}\text{ }\operatorname{ln}⁡2+\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡10}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Slope of the Tangent Line of a Logarithmic Function at a Point
questions.problem: Given that $y=3\operatorname{log}⁡x+{x}^{3}-4$, find the slope of the tangent at $x=3.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{3}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡10}+3{x}^{2}\,.
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=3} & ={(\frac{3}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡10}+3{x}^{2})|}_{x=3} \\  & =\frac{3}{3\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡10}+3\cdot {3}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡10}+27\,.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating a Logarithmic Function With a General Base
questions.problem:
Given the function  $y=2{log}_{3}⁡x-4\operatorname{ln}⁡x+5{e}^{x},$ find the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1.$ Do not round the answer.

The instantaneous rate of change at $x=1$ is
{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
To differentiate a logarithm with base $a,$ we use the formula

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{a}⁡x)=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡a}.
$$

To find the instantaneous rate of change at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{log}_{3}⁡x-4\operatorname{ln}⁡x+5{e}^{x}) \\  & =\frac{2}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\frac{4}{x}+5{e}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(\frac{2}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\frac{4}{x}+5{e}^{x})\,|}_{x=1} \\  & =\frac{2}{1\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\frac{4}{1}+5{e}^{1} \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-4+5e\,.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating a Sum Containing a Natural Logarithm Function
questions.problem:
Given the function  $y=-3\operatorname{ln}⁡x+2{e}^{x}+4$, find the instantaneous rate of change at $x=2.$ Do not round the answer.

The instantaneous rate of change at $x=2$ is
{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
To find the instantaneous rate of change at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-3\operatorname{ln}⁡x+2{e}^{x}+4) \\  & =-\frac{3}{x}+2{e}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change at $x=2$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=2} & ={(-\frac{3}{x}+2{e}^{x})|}_{x=2} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}+2{e}^{2}\,.\end{aligned}
$$
